# Generated files

This page lists the files `Generate` writes, when it refuses to write them, the per-file generator methods, and the modules the generated code imports, for a developer wiring wiregen's output into a TypeScript build.

## What Generate writes

`(*Registry).Generate(ctx, outDir)` writes these files to `outDir`, under the names the options set:

| File | Written when |
| --- | --- |
| `types.gen.ts` | always |
| `decoders.gen.ts` | always |
| `registry.gen.ts` | `SSEEvents` is non-empty |
| `constants.gen.ts` | `Constants` is non-empty |
| `client.gen.ts` | `Endpoints` is non-empty, see [Typed HTTP client](http-client.md) |
| the validators module | `WithValidatorsFile` is set |
| the arbitraries module | `WithArbitrariesFile` is set, see [Property-test arbitraries](arbitraries.md) |

Every file starts with the header comment, `// CODE-GENERATED by wiregen, DO NOT EDIT.` unless `WithHeaderComment` changes it.

## Errors and writing

`Generate` builds every file in memory first. It returns an error and writes nothing in these cases:

- `ValidatorsImport` is empty.
- `BusImport` is empty while SSE events are registered and the registry is not self-contained.
- `TransportImport` is empty while endpoints are registered.
- One bare type name is registered twice. Types are keyed by bare name, so two same-named types from different packages are rejected too.
- Two enums resolve to the same TypeScript type name or the same value-array name.
- A `WireConst`'s `TSName` has no characters left once it is cleaned to a TypeScript identifier.
- The endpoint table is invalid, see [Typed HTTP client](http-client.md#validation).
- A `//wiregen:union` type is registered in `SSEEvents` without a `DiscriminatorMap` entry.
- The registered packages fail to load or type-check.

Each file is then staged as a temporary file beside its target and renamed into place. A staging failure, such as a full disk, leaves the directory untouched. The renames run one after another, so a failure partway through can leave a mix of old and new files. Each file on its own is always either the old version or the new one.

`ctx` bounds the package load, which runs the `go` command as a subprocess. Cancelling it stops the pass, and the cancellation reason, including a cause set with `context.WithCancelCause`, is reachable with `errors.Is`.

## Generator methods

Each method returns one file's content without writing anything. Every one that can fail returns an error for the same configuration problems `Generate` rejects, and none panics.

- `GenerateTypes(ctx) (string, error)`: the types file.
- `GenerateDecoders(ctx) (string, error)`: the decoders file. Errors when `ValidatorsImport` is empty.
- `GenerateArbitraries(ctx) (string, error)`: the fast-check arbitraries module.
- `GenerateRegistry() (string, error)`: the registry file. Errors when `BusImport` is empty on a registry that is not self-contained, or when `ValidatorsImport` is empty on one that is.
- `GenerateConstants() (string, error)`: the constants file. Errors on a `TSName` that cleans to nothing.
- `GenerateClient() (string, error)`: the typed client. Errors when `TransportImport` or `ValidatorsImport` is empty, or the endpoint table is invalid.
- `GenerateGoPaths(pkgName string) (string, error)`: a gofmt-formatted Go file with one `Path*` constant per endpoint. Errors on an invalid endpoint table or package name.
- `GenerateValidators() string`: the validators module. Its body does not depend on the registered types, and the configured header is the only registry-specific part, so it cannot fail.

The four methods that take a context, `Generate` included, are exactly the four that read the registered packages from source. The rest render from the registry alone and do no I/O.

## Validators module

The decoders import their checks by name from the module at `ValidatorsImport`. wiregen writes that module, so you never edit it. Set `WithValidatorsFile` so `Generate` rewrites it on every run and it always matches the decoders. `GenerateValidators()` returns the same content for a generator that writes the file itself. Your own hand-written decoders may import and build on the same helpers.

A failed check throws a `TypeError` whose message starts with the JSON path, such as `$.user.id: expected number, got string`. `decodeArray` and `decodeRecord` add the element index or key to the path. The module exports:

- `asObject(v: unknown, path = "$"): Record<string, unknown>`
- `asArray(v: unknown, path = "$"): unknown[]`
- `reqStr(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$"): string`
- `reqNum(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$"): number`, which rejects `NaN` and `Infinity`
- `reqBool(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$"): boolean`
- `optStr(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$"): string | undefined`
- `optNum(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$"): number | undefined`
- `optBool(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$"): boolean | undefined`
- `reqOneOf<T extends string>(o: Record<string, unknown>, key: string, vals: readonly T[], path = "$"): T`
- `decodeArray<T>(v: unknown, decode: Decoder<T>, path = "$"): T[]`
- `decodeRecord<T>(v: unknown, decode: Decoder<T>, path = "$"): Record<string, T>`
- `type Decoder<T> = (v: unknown) => T`

## SSE registry and bus module

With `SSEEvents` registered, `registry.gen.ts` exports one function, `registerAllSSEDecoders()` by default, that binds each event name to its decoder. It works in one of two ways:

- By default it imports `registerSSEDecoder` from your bus module at `WithBusImport` and calls `registerSSEDecoder(eventType, decoder)` once per event. Your bus module decides what to do with each pair, such as decoding the `data` of each `EventSource` message by its event type.
- With `WithSelfContainedRegistry(true)` it keeps the pairs in its own `Map` and also exports `getSSEDecoder(eventType: string): Decoder<unknown> | undefined`. No bus module is needed.

`WithRegisterFuncName` and `WithRegistryFuncName` rename the two functions.
